name: versions

steps.action: C26 step 2-4: Upload one file, read the v1 row and its filename-derived name
steps.actual: Guide step 2-4 followed in the browser: one file created one Document titled from its filename, showing v1, the chosen Draft · ours kind and the typed note

steps.action: C26 step 2 variant: choosing several files opens the bulk import dialog instead of the composer
steps.actual: Picking two files in the Upload composer replaced it with the Import 2 files dialog, exactly as the guide warns; Cancel created nothing

steps.action: C26 step 5-7: Add version appends v2 and the earlier round stays readable and unchanged
steps.actual: Add version raised the chain to v2; expanding the row opened v1 in its own reader with the earlier note, kind, filename and author intact

steps.action: C26: the same paper uploaded again is a separate chain, not a merge
steps.actual: Re-uploading identical bytes as a new Document produced a second one-round chain; OpenLaw merged nothing, as the guide states

steps.action: C26: Edit details renames the Document and adds a description without touching the chain
steps.actual: Actions > Edit details > Save changed the logical name and description; both immutable Versions and their original filenames survived

steps.action: C26: a hand-set kind can be corrected, Generated redline is not offered, and the pin is untouched
steps.actual: The Kind control offered the six hand-set kinds only; correcting v2 to Amendment left the Version id, bytes and executed pin exactly as they were

steps.action: C26: Mark as executed copy pins an earlier Version and a later upload does not move the pin
steps.actual: The pin was set on the older v1 from the expanded chain; a fresh v3 upload became current but left the executed-copy designation on v1, as the guide states

steps.action: C26: Make primary moves the designation between separate Documents
steps.actual: Make primary moved the single Primary mark to another Document; both chains kept every Version, matching the guide’s separate-designation wording

steps.action: C26: a Matter offers no primary or executed-copy control
steps.actual: On a Matter the row menu offered Add version, Edit details, Move to folder and Archive but neither designation item, as the guide says

steps.action: C26 negative: an archived owning record takes no new paper until it is restored
steps.actual: On the archived Contract the Documents tab offered no Upload control at all; restoring the record brought it straight back, matching the guide’s recovery advice
